controls.qwen: RANA Q6_K, context 262144, target KV f16

limits: Sampled fixture minima are not a universal throughput guarantee.
Startup memory and available RAM include allocator and system cache variation.
Different output hashes prevent a claim of identical numerical behavior.
No broad accuracy or long-running concurrency validation.
Vision read-byte differences include OS page-cache warming; they are not attributed to the profile.

experiments.error: RuntimeError({'type': 'server_error', 'message': 'the engine stopped unexpectedly (exit code -6); the next request restarts it'})

qwen.action: retain production Vulkan, Q4_K_M DFlash2, depth 4
qwen.hip_note: Unmodified HIP failed its 16GiB KV allocation. The private allocator patch loaded 262K/f16 but measured 17.97/12.70 tok/s and 3.58GiB minimum available RAM; stopped after those two regressions.

flash.action: RAM profile reverted; retain the faster 4096 prefill baseline
flash.tradeoff: About 0.5-0.7GiB less startup cgroup memory; sampled decode similar; cold prefill about 10-11% lower throughput.
flash.why_duplicate: Prefill borrows GPU expert-cache slots. RAM backups restore overwritten experts without reading the pack again. Most of the 17.34GiB host complement is distinct experts, not duplicate GPU weights. Decode already uses a mapped host alias.
flash.rejected_resident_budget_16_gib: Saved about 1GiB startup cgroup memory but caused about 6.5GiB physical reads on every 16K request versus 33-39MiB on repeated control requests.
flash.rejected_ring_256: Engine exited -6 during the first 16K request; no new system OOM. Exact failure mechanism unproven.

io.limit: Process observations do not imply zero system-wide writes from journaling or other services.

deployment.status: historical RAM profile deployment; subsequently reverted

current_deployment.validation: Configuration matches the earlier measured 4096 baseline exactly. Engine health and router loaded/idle state checked; no new throughput benchmark in this rollback.

optimization_policy: Speed first for Flash and 27B. RAM savings are secondary and must not reduce measured prefill or decode performance.
